name: Sage
lede: Sage is the soft, greyish green of the leaves of the sage plant; most of the times books say "sage" they mean a wise person, which makes the color's own record unusually thin.

sections.title: The leaf
sections.body: Paterson defines sage-green as the greyish or yellowish green of the leaves of the sage plant, and sage-grey as a greyish olive [1][2]. Jarman's garden verse in *Chroma* lists sage among the healing herbs he planted, and adds that the plant's flowers are blue, so the color is the leaf's and not the flower's [3].

sections.title: Two meanings in the books
sections.body: Many mentions of sage in the color books are about people, not plants. Finlay quotes the twelfth-century sage Maimonides on the blue of the sea, sky and throne of God [4]. In French, *sage* means well-behaved, and Pastoureau calls blue a very *sage* color for that reason [5]. Neither has anything to do with the color; a search for the word finds mostly these [4][5].

sections.title: In color systems
sections.body: The library files Sage under ISCC-NBS 1955 block 120, with Ridgway's 1912 near-duplicate Mytho Green, plate XLI, a color distance (ΔE) of 1.5 away [6]. It lists two Maerz and Paul entries for the name, first recorded 1596 and 1912 [6]. Sources disagree on the swatch itself: the Wikipedia list gives #BCB88A, a yellower olive, and xkcd gives #87AE73, a brighter green, against our #9CAF88 [6]. See also [[sage-green]], [[olive-green]] and [[tea-green]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Sage is uncommon in painting as photographed: 134 of the 23,531 paintings in the archive carry a color this close, 0.56 percent [7]. Its measured lightness is 69, chroma 23 and hue 128 [6].
